description: Manual gold-standard diagnosis. Arabic-first home water-filter brand (نقاء / Naqaa), first_purchase decision, persuasion bottleneck. Two competitors. Built to the frozen schemas so a human can diagnose it and automated checks can verify evidence linkage, verbatim spans, canonical enums, and separate severity/confidence.

project.name: Naqaa Home Water Filter — First Purchase

context_version.target_buying_decision: Household buys its first Naqaa under-sink water filter (first_purchase).
context_version.primary_product_or_service: Under-sink home water filtration unit with annual cartridge plan.
context_version.primary_segment_definition: Parents in GCC/Egyptian cities worried about tap-water quality for their children.
context_version.bottleneck_statement: Prospects believe filters are expensive and hard to maintain, and doubt the long-term value versus bottled water.

entities.name: AquaPure
entities.comparison_rationale: Direct competitor selling the same under-sink category to the same urban families.

entities.comparison_rationale: Indirect substitute: bottled-water subscription competing for the same budget.

expected_gaps.title: No proven long-term cost justification vs bottled water at the persuasion touchpoint
expected_gaps.customer_need: Proof that the filter saves money long-term versus buying bottled water.
expected_gaps.required_coverage_description: A documented 3-year cost comparison with real numbers, at the evaluation touchpoint, with proof.
expected_gaps.alternative_explanation: The brand may have the numbers internally but has never documented them (extraction_gap) rather than lacking a real cost advantage.

expected_gaps.title: Weak installation-simplicity coverage at the evaluation stage
expected_gaps.customer_need: Reassurance that installation is simple and does not require a technician.
expected_gaps.required_coverage_description: A step-by-step installation walkthrough addressing the difficulty objection.
expected_gaps.alternative_explanation: Installation content may exist but be hard to find (distribution_gap).

expected_gaps.title: Generic 'benefits of water' territory competitors publish heavily with no first-party demand
expected_gaps.customer_need: None evidenced — no VoC, journey, or performance evidence supports importance for the decision.
expected_gaps.required_coverage_description: Not required; publishing more generic benefit content would not move the first-purchase decision.
expected_gaps.alternative_explanation: Competitor volume here is promotional noise, not decision support.

expected_gaps.title: White space: Arabic proof-backed installation-plus-savings walkthrough owned by nobody
expected_gaps.customer_need: One Arabic asset that proves both easy installation and long-term savings together.
expected_gaps.required_coverage_description: A combined proof asset; requires confirming the brand has a credible proof path.
expected_gaps.alternative_explanation: The territory may be small; importance must be confirmed against VoC before owning it.

expected_gaps.title: No defined installation-service SLA — content cannot promise easy installation yet
expected_gaps.customer_need: A reliable installation service before content can credibly promise simple setup.
expected_gaps.required_coverage_description: Define and staff an installation SLA; then content can address the objection truthfully.
expected_gaps.alternative_explanation: If an SLA already exists but is undocumented, this is an extraction_gap, not an operational one.
